figures.finding: Under the Employment Act Part 8 and the Employment of Children and Young Persons Regulations, a child of thirteen to under fifteen may do light duties in a non-industrial setting and industrial work only with family members; a young person of fifteen to under sixteen may work in either, the employer notifying MOM with a medical report within thirty days for industrial work; nothing is allowed below thirteen.

value.industrialNotice: MOM notice and medical report within 30 days (15 to under 16)

figures.applies: Employment Act 1968 Part 8; Employment of Children and Young Persons Regulations, as MOM states them.

sources.said: The type of work children and young persons can do is governed by Part 8 of the Employment Act and the Employment of Children and Young Persons Regulations . ... Children aged 13 to less than 15 years ... Yes, for light duties only. ... No, unless working with family members. ... Young persons aged 15 to less than 16 years ... Yes. ... Yes, but employers must notify MOM and submit a medical report within 30 days of starting work.

figures.finding: MOM names no permit or exception for child performers: the general rules apply, so a child of thirteen to fifteen may do only light duties outside industrial settings and none is allowed under thirteen (reading of MOM's table; whether the Regulations exempt performing wasn't read, the statute site being closed to this agent). For manual labour, children and young persons can't work 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. or on rest days without the Commissioner's leave; a child no more than three hours without a thirty-minute break or six hours a day including school, a young person four and seven. The same reaches a child writer or director employed (reading).

sources.said: The type of work children and young persons can do is governed by Part 8 of the Employment Act and the Employment of Children and Young Persons Regulations . ... Children aged 13 to less than 15 years ... Yes, for light duties only. ... No, unless working with family members. ... Young persons aged 15 to less than 16 years ... Yes. ... Yes, but employers must notify MOM and submit a medical report within 30 days of starting work.

They cannot work at night, between 11pm and 6am the next day. ... They cannot work on their rest days without permission from the Commissioner for Labour. ... Children must not work: ... More than 3 hours without a 30-minute break. ... More than 6 hours in a day, including time at school. ... Young persons must not work: ... More than 4 hours without a 30-minute break. ... More than 7 hours in a day, including time at school.
